description: Fermi estimate of a public CBAM calculation tool: Expected-value estimate for building a public, source-bound CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) calculation tool, conditional on the stated premise that a usable tool causes an additional 10% reduction in global GHG emissions within one year.

words.name: adoption
words.description: use of the tool by importers, authorities or civil society

words.name: build
words.description: the one-off creation of the tool

words.name: confidence
words.description: Subjective probability (0 to 1) that the tagged estimate range contains the true value.

words.name: effect-relevant
words.description: at a scale sufficient to plausibly drive the assumed emissions effect, e.g. integrated into EU CBAM reporting workflows or widely used by importers and civil society

words.name: GtCO2eq
words.description: Is a symbol for gigatonnes of CO2 equivalent

words.name: usable
words.description: the tool is technically functional AND adopted at a scale sufficient to plausibly drive the assumed emissions effect; bundles technical completion and adoption

words.name: value
words.description: a stored number; reference the provenance qualifier triple, not this bare word

triples.name: public CBAM calculation tool
triples.description: Publicly usable, source-verifiable tool for calculating carbon-border-adjustment obligations, in the zukunft.com sense of numbers bound to word/triple/source chains

triples.name: greenhouse gas emission
triples.description: Release of a greenhouse gas into the atmosphere.

triples.name: global greenhouse gas emissions
triples.description: Total global greenhouse gas emissions, all sectors including LULUCF

triples.name: social cost of carbon
triples.description: EPA 2023 central estimate, 2020 USD per metric ton CO2, 2% near-term discount rate

triples.name: causal chain
triples.description: The assumed mechanism: public tool -> supply-chain transparency -> closes carbon-leakage gap -> changes importer behavior -> tightens policy -> global emissions effect. Stated as a premise by the user, NOT independently derived or verified here.

triples.name: build cost
triples.description: one-off cost of building the tool

triples.name: technical completion
triples.description: the tool is finished and technically functional

triples.name: effect-relevant adoption
triples.description: the finished tool is adopted widely enough to drive the assumed emissions effect
US dollars per metric tonne of CO2, in 2020 USD at a 2 percent near-term discount rate

triples.name: confidence value
triples.description: The p-value of an assumed value: the subjective probability between 0 and 1 that the tagged estimate is right.

values.description: range 120-340 USD/t depending on discount rate (2.5%/2.0%/1.5%)
values.source: EPA Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, Dec 2023

values.description: User-stated premise, taken as given for this model; not derived from an independent causal chain. This is the single largest source of uncertainty in the whole estimate and should be its own decomposed sub-model.
2 developers + 1 trade/carbon-accounting domain expert + 1 policy/legal, 18 months, plus data licensing/verification infrastructure
conditional on technical completion; largest source of adoption uncertainty

formula: EV = P(usable) * (0.10 * global_emissions_2024 * SCC) - build_cost, where P(usable) = P(technical completion) * P(adoption)

result.expected_value_note: One-year, non-compounding effect only, per the stated premise. If the effect is assumed durable/annual, NPV over 10y at 5% discount scales roughly x7.7.
result.sensitivity: Cost-effectiveness case (build_cost vs. EV) is positive even at P(usable) as low as 0.0001 (EV ~110M USD, still >>build_cost). The result is therefore almost entirely determined by the 10 percent causal premise, not by cost or adoption probability.
